transcript:

Most enterprises can't count their AI agents, let alone manage them.
DataIku Agent Management lets you do both from a single view.
Visit DataIku.com to learn more.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vekulman.
Stocks open mixed this morning as oil prices climb.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones Industrial Average
slipped nearly 200 points in early trading.
Crude oil prices inched higher with the international benchmark once again topping $100 a barrel.
Retail gasoline prices in the U.S. dipped overnight.
AAA says the average price of regular gas is now $4.41 a gallon.
The average price of diesel fuel is $6.38.
About a third of the states in the country have reduced or suspended their gasoline tax
in an effort to give drivers some short-term relief.
Ohio lawmakers voted yesterday to lift that state's gas tax for 90 days.
And Keith Sonderling will keep his job as U.S. Labor Secretary.
The Senate confirmed Sonderling's appointment on Wednesday.
He's been acting secretary for the last five months.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The government of the United Arab Emirates says it has opened an investigation into what
happened on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv following its emergency landing yesterday.
The UAE says prosecutors are looking into whether the incident is linked to terrorist
activity.
And it appears Ea Betrawi has more.
The flight of a plane was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers when it made an emergency
landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday following what the airline says was an altercation in
the cockpit.
Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says one of the pilots stabbed the other.
Saudi Arabia confirms both pilots were hospitalized.
President Trump says he was updated about the plane's emergency landing by Netanyahu.
Netanyahu, who's facing a tough re-election this month centered around security, was filmed
meeting an Israeli passenger after their arrival to Tel Aviv last night.
The passenger is seen telling Netanyahu how he got into the cockpit, put the attacker
in a choke hold, and pulled on the control stick to stop the plane from nose-diving.
Fly Dubai suspended all flights to Tel Aviv following the incident.
Ea Betrawi, NPR News, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
One of Iraq's most powerful militias backed by Iran says it will stop its attacks.
And it appears Jane Arav reports from Baghdad the U.S. military withdrew from Iraq yesterday.
Khattab Hezbollah said in a statement that the Islamic resistance had won this round
against what it called the U.S. occupation.
The U.S. on Wednesday announced it had withdrawn its military forces and closed the headquarters
here of an anti-ISIS coalition it has led since 2014.
The Islamic resistance is a grouping of Iran-backed militias that have frequently claimed attacks
against U.S. targets in Iraq.
Khattab Hezbollah directed its fighters to stop all attacks, apart from targeting aircraft
violating Iraqi airspace.
Jane Arav, NPR News, Baghdad.
Stocks had turned negative on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones industrials are now down 226 points.
This is NPR.
The state of Tennessee botched the execution of convicted murderer Christa Pike last night.
Executioners gave her a lethal dose of drugs twice.
Both attempts failed.
Witnesses say Pike was alive and snoring.
Tennessee officials have moved her to a hospital.
Pennsylvania health officials confirmed a fifth measles-associated death.
As NPR's Maria Godoy reports, this occurred in an unvaccinated person in Lancaster County,
the epicenter of the state's fast-growing measles outbreak.
This is the third death reported in recent weeks in Lancaster County and the fifth overall
in the state.
No additional details about the individual were released.
Pennsylvania has confirmed 943 measles cases so far this year, including 40 new cases in
the last two days alone.
However, experts say the true number of infections is likely much larger because people with milder
cases may not seek treatment, so their cases are never formally reported.
This is one of the most contagious diseases known.
It kills roughly one to three out of every 1,000 people infected, according to the National
Foundation for Infectious Diseases.
Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97 percent effective at preventing an infection.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
There are flood watches and warnings across much of the central U.S. today.
The remnants of a hurricane that hit Mexico are streaming north.
There are flash flood warnings scattered across parts of Texas, Oklahoma and Iowa.
SpaceX has scheduled a Florida launch later this morning of its Crew-13 mission.
The crew is scheduled to go to the International Space Station.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Stock markets open mixed as oil prices climb above $100 per barrel benchmark
U.S. retail gasoline prices dip to $4.41 per gallon average, diesel at $6.38
Ohio lawmakers vote to suspend state gasoline tax for 90 days
Keith Sonderling confirmed by Senate as U.S. Labor Secretary
UAE investigates emergency landing of Dubai to Tel Aviv flight, explores terrorism link
Passenger subdues pilot in cockpit altercation on flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv
Fly Dubai suspends all flights to Tel Aviv following cockpit incident
Iran-backed Iraqi militia Khattab Hezbollah announces halt to attacks on U.S. forces
U.S. military withdraws from Iraq, closes anti-ISIS coalition headquarters
Tennessee execution of Christa Pike fails twice, inmate transferred to hospital
Pennsylvania confirms fifth measles-associated death in unvaccinated person in Lancaster County
Pennsylvania reports 943 measles cases this year with outbreak accelerating
Flood watches and warnings issued across central U.S. from Mexican hurricane remnants
SpaceX scheduled to launch Crew-13 mission to International Space Station from Florida
